title: Nordskog, the singers and the Spikes brothers
summary: Garland dealt only with the Spikes brothers; the two girls sang Spikes numbers; what became of the brothers; session timing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Just one of them things. We just stayed right there. Well, who was this guy, Northscog? Who? Northscog. Did you know a guy called Northscog? Because some of those records came out on the Northscog label. No. You didn't know Northscog. No, no, no. The only man you dealt with was the Spikes brothers. Spikes brothers, that's who we dealt with.
The two girls sing and we six played.
Well, the two girls who sang, did they bring in those girls or did you know those girls?
No, I know. But I mean,
it was their idea. I mean, those girls didn't sing with Ori's band, in other words.
No, no, no, no. They sang Spikes numbers.
Remember Spikes numbers, Johnny, you know, and Rebs. That was Josh Rebs number. Are they still living,

Are they both living? No, John and the Spikes, uh, Rebs, Rebs living in the real estate business. Here in town. Do you ever see him? I've seen him quite a while. He's on Western Avenue. Western Avenue near, uh,
29th. So, the studio, when do you make him? In the afternoon? Or at night?
Do you remember what time? In the day, around 11 o'clock or something.
Somebody told me a story that Ori came in with a black tie for that session. Is that true?
No, no, no. For the black tie, let's do it. If it was, it was a fooling hand. Not no bow tie.
No, and I don't think he come in with no black tie. Not that. Because, uh, we had our coach and all.
